column1: Okay, well the action of G on a set is the same thing as giving a homomorphism from G into the symmetric group of the set: it takes an element g and sends it to the permutation s goes to g(s). That's what an action of a group is on a set: it's a group homomorphism.
column2: 好，群 G 在集合上的作用，完全等价于给出一个从 G 到该集合对称群的同态；它把元素 g 映为置换 s ↦ g(s)。这就是群在集合上的作用：它是一个群同态。

column1: And since the set has n elements, the symmetry group is the same as the symmetric group on n letters S_n, and this is a group of order n!.
column2: 因为集合有 n 个元素，其对称群也就是 n 个文字上的对称群 S_n，其阶数为 n!。

column1: Now it doesn't mean that this is an injection or anything like that, it's just a homomorphism: to every element in the group G you get a permutation, and when you compose elements in the group, you compose permutations.
column2: 这并不意味着它是单射或别的什么，它仅仅是一个同态：对 G 中的每个元素都对应一个置换，群中复合元素就对应置换的复合。

column1: Okay, but if we have a homomorphism from a group of order greater than n! to a group of order n!, it has to have a kernel, because whatever the size of the image is in here, it has order dividing n!, and the order of the image times the order of the kernel has to be the order of G.
column2: 好，但是如果我们有一个从阶数大于 n! 的群到阶数为 n! 的群的同态，它必然具有非平凡的核，因为无论这里的像有多大，其阶数都整除 n!，而像的阶乘以核的阶必须等于G 的阶。

Since G acts non-trivially, the kernel of rho is not equal to G.

column1: Okay, some people did it without the whole homomorphism thing, and they said—and this is just as good—they said: look, I have more than n! elements here, I have n! elements here; by the pigeonhole principle, if I have a map from this set to this set, two elements in this set have to go to the same permutation.

So the order of G is equal to the sum of the orders of all the conjugacy classes, and we break this sum into the conjugacy classes that have one element and the ones that have more than one element; and the ones that have one element are just the elements of the center.

column1: But for five, if you have R[x] and you want to give a surjective homomorphism from R[x] to R, for the homomorphism, you take a polynomial f(x) and you send it to the value of the polynomial at 1: f(1).
column2: 但在第五题中，如果你有多项式环 R[x]，想给出一个映到 R 的满同态，对于这个同态，你取一个多项式 f(x)，将它映为该多项式在 1 处的取值 f(1)。

column1: That is a ring homomorphism, because if you add two polynomials, you add their values at 1; and if you multiply two polynomials and you evaluate at 1, you multiply the values at 1.
column2: 这是一个环同态，因为两多项式相加，其在 1 处的值相加；两多项式相乘在 1 处求值，也就是在 1 处的取值相乘。

column1: So that's a ring homomorphism, and it has the property that h of the polynomial x - 1 is equal to 0, so h of any multiple of x - 1, h is equal to 0, because it's a homomorphism.
column2: 所以这是环同态，且它满足 h(x - 1) = 0，从而对 x - 1 的任意倍式，h 也都等于 0，因为它是同态。

column1: So the ideal (x - 1) is in the kernel of h, and that means that it induces a homomorphism of this quotient ring into the ring R. And it's surjective, because anything can be the value of f(1): just take any constant polynomial to its value.
column2: 所以理想 (x - 1) 包含在 ker h 中，这意味着它诱导了从商环 R[x]/(x-1) 到环 R 的同态。而且它是满射，因为 R 中的任意元素都可以是 f(1) 的值：只要取任意常数多项式即可映到该常数值。

column1: So that's the proof that you have a surjective homomorphism from this to the ring.

column1: Okay, good, and then the second part is to show that this is actually an isomorphism, namely if f(1) is equal to 0, then you're in the ideal (x - 1).

column1: To show h is an isomorphism, we must show that when f(1) = 0, f(x) = (x - 1) g(x), namely that the kernel of this map is exactly the principal ideal generated by x - 1.

column1: And for this we use the Euclidean algorithm, which says we can take any polynomial f(x) and write it as (x - 1) g(x) plus a constant, which is a polynomial of degree less than the degree of x - 1.
column2: 为此我们要用欧几里得除法（带余除法），它指出我们可以取任意多项式 f(x)，写成 (x - 1)g(x) 加一个常数 c，常数的次数小于 x - 1 的次数。

column1: And you can do that because this is a monic polynomial; and then we find that f(1) is equal to 0 * g(1) + c, which means that the value f(1) is c.
column2: 你能够做除法是因为 x - 1 是首一多项式；然后我们发现 f(1) = 0 · g(1) + c，这意味着 f(1) 的值就是 c。

column1: So that if f(1) = 0, it says this c = 0, which means that f of x is divisible by x - 1.
column2: 因此若 f(1) = 0，就意味着 c = 0，从而 f(x)可被 x - 1 整除。

column1: So six: we have G of order pq where p < q. So we have a Sylow subgroup of order q: a Sylow q-subgroup.
column2: 第六题：设群 G 的阶为 pq，其中 p < q。那么有一个阶为q 的西罗子群——西罗 q-子群。

column1: And all are conjugate, so it will be normal if it's unique.
column2: 所有西罗 q-子群都共轭，所以只要唯一就是正规子群。

column1: Well, the number of Sylow q-subgroups has the property that it divides p, and it's congruent to 1 mod q. And since p < q, the only number that divides p and leaves a remainder of 1 mod q is 1.
column2: 而西罗 q-子群的个数满足：它整除 p，并且模 q 同余于 1。又因为 p < q，整除 p 且模 q余 1 的数只能是 1。

column1: So this number has to be 1. Consequently, the Sylow q-subgroup is unique, consequently it's normal.
column2: 所以这个数目必定是 1。从而西罗 q-子群唯一，进而正规。

column1: And the extra credit problem: suppose you assume further that your prime p does not divide q - 1.
column2: 至于附加题：假设进一步假定素数 p 不整除 q- 1。

column1: Then in fact the Sylow p-subgroup is actually a normal subgroup in G.
column2: 那么事实上西罗 p-子群也是 G 的正规子群。

column1: That's unusual, but it occurs here, because the number of Sylow p-subgroups divides q, and it's congruent to 1 mod p—that's by the Sylow theorems. On the other hand, the only numbers that divide a prime q are q and 1.
column2: 这很不寻常，但在本条件下确实成立，因为西罗 p-子群的个数整除 q，且模 p 同余于 1——这是由西罗定理保证的。另一方面，能整除素数 q 的数只有 q 和 1。

column1: q is not congruent to 1 mod p, because that's our hypothesis: that p does not divide q - 1. So therefore the only number that divides q and is congruent to 1 mod p is 1, which says that S_p is normal in G.

column1: Well, how does that prove that the group is cyclic? Well, think about it: what are the possible orders of elements in a group of order pq?

column1: How many elements are there of order q? Well, any element of order q generates a Sylow q-subgroup. There's a unique Sylow q- subgroup, right?

column1: So there are exactly q - 1 elements of order q in this group. So let's put that down: q - 1 elements of order q. Any element of order p generates a Sylow p-subgroup; but in this case there's a unique Sylow p-subgroup, so there are p - 1 elements of order p.

column2: 因此我们已经统计的元素总数是 p + q - 1 个 G 的元素。然而 G 的总阶数是pq，对吧？

column1: Now I claim that this number is strictly less than that number. Why?
column2: 现在我断言：这个数字严格小于 pq。为什么？

column2: 因为 p + q - 1 显然小于 p +q，而 p + q 显然小于 2q，因为 q > p，对吧？

column1: And 2q is certainly less than or equal to p * q, because whatever p is, it's >= 2: it's a prime! And so this number is strictly less than that number.
column2: 且 2q 显然小于等于 p ·q，因为无论 p 是多少，作为素数它都 ≥ 2！所以这个数目严格小于全群的阶数。

column1: Okay, so we say a ring, a commutative ring is an integral domain—or sometimes we'll just use the word domain to be short—if it has the following property: whenever a * b = 0 in R, then either a = 0 or b = 0 in R.

column1: Namely, you can't have a product which is zero without it being a trivial product which is zero: one of the elements is zero. So those are called domains.

column2: 显然成立的是每个符号与自身等价，所以满足自反性；而且如果 a/b 与a'/b' 等价，那么 a'/b' 也与 a/b 等价——这是由环的乘法交换律保证的。好，关键需要验证的是传递性。

column1: So suppose that a'/b' is equivalent on the other hand to a''/b''; so that would say that a' b'' is equal to b' a''. And somehow I have to get... so I have this equivalence, I have this equivalence; I want to show that a/b and a''/b'' are actually equivalent.
column2: 假设 a'/b' 另一方面又与 a''/b'' 等价；这就意味着 a' b'' = b' a''。而我必须推导出……我已知这两个等价式，想要证明 a/b 与 a''/b'' 事实上也是等价的。

column1: Okay, so now there's a trick: you have to multiply by something, which I'm going to look up, and since I've changed notation I'll undoubtedly get it wrong!

column2: 然后我想把第二个式子乘以——大家有什么想法？乘 b？我们试试乘 b。好的，那么这变成了 b a' b'' = b b' a''。好，

column1: now let's see if we can get something out of this. So here I have... ah, so this quantity b a' b'' here is equal to this quantity here; it's the same three symbols!
column2: 现在来看看能否从中得出结论。所以这里我有……啊，所以这里的 b a' b'' 等于这里的这一项；它们是完全相同的三个符号！

column1: Okay, therefore this number is equal to this number: a b' b'' = b b' a''.
column2: 好，因此这个数等于那个数：a b' b'' = b b' a''。

column1: On the other hand, I now use the cancellation law, that both of these things are multiplied by b', and b' prime is not equal to 0, because it was one of the denominators. So I can cancel by something that's not equal to 0!
column2: 另一方面，我现在使用消去律：两边都乘以了 b'，而 b'不等于 0，因为它是其中一个分母。所以我可以消去一个非零元素！

column1: So cancel the b' to get a b'' = b a'', which is the fact that this fraction a/b is equivalent to this fraction a''/b''.
column2: 于是消去 b' 得到 a b'' = b a''，而这正是分数 a/b与分数 a''/b'' 等价的充要条件！

column1: Tricky, huh? So again, we've used domain right there in the cancellation, to show that this is an equivalence relation.
column2: 很巧妙吧？所以我们在这里再次用到了整环的消去律，来证明这是一个等价关系。

column1: And now we define—and this is what's totally cool—F to be the set S modulo the equivalence relation: the set of equivalence classes of fractions with this relation.
column2: 现在我们定义——这也是极妙之处——F 为集合 S 模去该等价关系所得的商集：即满足此等价关系的由分式构成的等价类集合。

column1: Now that looks good, that looks promising; I mean, that's what we really do for rational numbers if you think about it: if you try to describe to people why 1/3 is equal to 2/6, it's that you have a bunch of symbols, some of which are equal to some other symbols.
column2: 这看起来很好，很有希望；如果你仔细想想，这正是我们对有理数所做的事情：如果你尝试向人解释为什么 1/3 等于 2/6，其实就是你有一堆符号，其中一些与另一些符号等价。

column1: But it doesn't solve our problem yet, because we now have to show that this has the structure of a field which contains the domain R.

column1: Okay, so let's add and multiply: so suppose we have a/b, and we want to add it to the symbol c/d; and then we also have to tell you what a/b times the symbol c/d is; and then we have to tell you what (a/b)^{-1} is, things like that.
column2: 好，我们来定义加法与乘法：假设我们有 a/b，想将它与符号 c/d 相加；然后我们还得规定符号 a/b 乘以符号 c/d 是什么；接着还得告诉你 (a/b)^{-1}是什么，诸如此类。

column1: Okay, well, this is where you go back to third grade: this is equal to (ad + bc)/bd, that's by definition—we're going to check that that definition works; and this symbol is (ac)/(bd) by definition; and this inverse symbol is b/a.
column2: 好，这里就要回到小学三年级了：按定义，这等于 (ad + bc)/bd——我们将验证这个定义是行得通的；乘积符号按定义是 (ac)/(bd)；而这个逆元符号是 b/a。

column1: You can only do this if a is not equal to 0, otherwise you're inverting 0, okay?
column2: 只有当a ≠ 0 时才能求逆，否则你就是在对零求逆，对吧？

column1: Now notice, so far I'm okay: these are permissible symbols because b and d were non-zero, so their product is non- zero—again using the fact that I'm in a domain: I'm only allowed to put something that's non-zero in the denominator.
column2: 现在请注意，到目前为止都没问题：这些都是合法的符号，因为 b 和 d 非零，所以它们的乘积也非零——再次用到了我们在整环中的事实：分母上只允许放入非零元素。

column1: So this is a symbol, this is a symbol, and this is a symbol if a != 0, which is when I'm going to make an inversion.
column2: 所以这是一个合法符号，这是一个合法符号，且当 a ≠ 0 时这也是合法符号，此时我才求逆。

column2: 而且这个符号满足性质：当把它乘以 a/b 时，得到 ab/ab，它等价于 1/1。

column1: I should say how R maps into this field, by the way: R goes into F by taking an element a and sending it to the symbol a/1.
column2: 顺便说一下 R 是如何嵌入到这个域中的：R 映入 F 的方式是把元素 a 映为符号a/1。

column1: That's a perfectly good symbol, because 1 != 0 in a domain; the zero ring is not a domain, doesn't count.
column2: 这是一个完全合法的符号，因为在整环中 1 ≠ 0；零环不是整环，不算在内。

column1: Okay, now this isn't done yet, this is far from being done; this is just the beginning! And the reason is that you have to check that this is well-defined.
column2: 好，现在构造还没完成，远远没有完成；这仅仅是刚开始！原因是：你必须验证它是良定义的。

column1: What do I mean by well-defined? Well, the elements of the field are not symbols, they're equivalence classes of symbols!
column2: 良定义是什么意思？域里的元素不是符号本身，而是符号的等价类！

column1: So you have to check that if you take another symbol: if a/b is equivalent to a'/b', and c/d is equivalent to c'/d', then you have to check that (ad + bc)/bd is itself equivalent to (a'd' + b'c') / (b'd').
column2: 所以你必须验证：如果取另一个等价的代表元：如果 a/b 等价于 a'/b'，且 c/d 等价于c'/d'，那么你必须验证 (ad + bc)/bd 本身等价于 (a'd' + b'c') / (b'd')。

column1: Namely, otherwise addition isn't well-defined: you could choose a different representative of your equivalence class and get a different answer.
column2: 换言之，否则加法就不是良定义的：你选取等价类的不同代表元，就会得到不同的运算结果。

column1: Okay, well again, if you believe that this works, it's just a matter... I mean, how hard can this be?
column2: 好，如果你相信这是成立的，这其实只是……我是说，这能有多难？

column1: You're not allowed to do any calculus here, you can't differentiate anything, so it has to be pretty simple! Let's see if we can do it, and I'll let you check some of the other things. So this says that ab' = ba', and this says that cd' = dc'.
column2: 这里又不允许用微积分，你又不能求导，所以肯定相当简单！我们来看看怎么做，剩下的细节留给大家自己检验。已知条件是 ab' = ba'，以及 cd' = dc'。

column2: 来看看，我认为其中一项直接相等：比如……大家帮我看看！对，第一项：这里有 a 和 b'——这里的 ab'——乘 dd'；而右边有 dd' ba'。

column1: Okay, good! So in fact this fraction is equivalent to this fraction, so this addition law makes sense.
column2: 好的！所以这两个分式确实是等价的，加法定义是良定义的。

column1: It's easier to check multiplication; and so this is really the mathematical generalization of the construction of the rational numbers.
column2: 乘法的良定义更容易验证；所以这确实是有理数构造的严格数学推广。

column1: And if you think about these other rings that I've mentioned: if you take elements like a + bi and you take fractions of the form (a + bi)/(c + di), well, 1/(c + di) can be written as (c - di)/(c^2 + d^2).
column2: 如果你回想我前面提到的那些环：如果你取类似 a + bi 的元素，考虑分式 (a + bi)/(c + di)，那么 1/(c + di) 可以写为 (c - di)/(c^2 + d^2)。

column1: So this element would be equivalent to (a + bi)(c - di) / (c^2 + d^2); and consequently here the coefficients in the numerator would all be integers, and you're just dividing by a non-zero integer, so this would be of the form alpha + beta i where alpha and beta are rational numbers.
column2: 所以这个数就等价于 (a + bi)(c - di) / (c^2 + d^2)；从而分子展开后的系数全都是整数，分母是一个非零整数，因此它必然形如 α + β i，其中 α, β 是有理数。

column1: So anything of this form in the Gaussian integers could be turned into something of this form where alpha and beta are rational numbers.
column2: 所以高斯整数中任何这种形式的分式都可以化为 α + β i 的形式，其中 α, β 为有理数。

column1: And likewise for the rational functions: I mean, if you just considered expressions A/B where A and B are polynomials and B != 0, that's exactly what a rational function is.
column2: 同理对于有理函数域：如果你考虑表达式 A/B，其中 A, B 是多项式且 B ≠ 0，这恰恰就是有理函数的定义。

column1: So there's really no mystery about this, but it's just such a cool construction that you can put a field structure on the set of these equivalence classes, whereas it would be extremely awkward to try to start talking about the original set itself.
column2: 所以这并没有什么深奥的秘密，但赋予这套等价类集合以域的结构是如此美妙的构造，而如果直接去讨论原来的符号集合本身就会极其笨拙。

column1: So this is a process in mathematics—a generalization which was developed a great deal in the '50s and '60s in ring theory—called "localization".
column2: 在数学中这是一个更广义的过程——在 50 和 60 年代的环论中得到了极大发展——被称为“局部化”（localization）。

column1: When you take Math 250, you'll spend huge amounts of time doing localization; but for all practical purposes, the construction of the quotient field is the main example of localization.
column2: 当大家上 Math 250 时，会花大量时间研究局部化；但在所有实际应用中，分式域（商域）是局部化最主要的例子。

column1: And now I'll show you what's so cool about the quotient field, and why it's the best field to construct.
column2: 现在我来向大家展示商域的精妙之处，以及为什么它是我们要构造的最理想的域。

column1: When you make a construction like this, you seem to make all kinds of arbitrary choices, and you don't know how to characterize what you've ended up with.
column2: 当你做这样一个构造时，表面上看似做了各种任意的选择，你不知道该如何刻画最终构造出的对象。

column1: So here's the characterization of the quotient field: the universal property: If R -> K is any ring inclusion into a field K, and F is the quotient field of R—so we have a natural inclusion R ↪ F—then there is a natural homomorphism of fields
column2: 这里给出了商域的特征刻画：泛性质（Universal Property）：若 R ↪ K 是环到域 K 的任意环包含嵌入，且 F 是 R 的商域——我们有自然的包含映射 R ↪ F——

column1: F -> K that makes the combination of these two maps equal to that one, so that any map from a ring into a field in some sense factors through its quotient field: first you put it in its quotient field, then you put the quotient field in the bigger field.
column2: 那么存在自然的域同态 F ↪ K 使得这两个映射的复合等于原嵌入，从而任何从环到域的映射在某种意义上都分解为经由其商域的映射：首先将它放入其商域，再把商域嵌入更大的域中。

column1: So for example, you could put the integers: the integers could certainly be put inside of Q(i), just as elements where the imaginary part is zero, right?
column2: 例如你可以把整数嵌入 Q(i)：整数当然可以放入 Q(i) 中，即虚部为零的数，对吧？

column1: But that would factor through the inclusion of the rationals Q into Q(i), and the map from the integers to its own quotient field Q.
column2: 但这会分解为有理数域 Q 在 Q(i) 中的包含，以及整数环到自身商域 Q 的映射。

column1: So it's sort of the smallest field that you can put R into. (Student: That homomorphism would also be injective?) Professor: Yes, that would also be injective: a homomorphism of fields is always injective.
column2: 所以它是在某种意义上能容纳 R 的最小的域。（学生：那这个同态也必然是单射吗？）教授：是的，它也是单射：域同态总是单射。

column1: I should have said that a homomorphism of fields is always injective, because remember that a homomorphism has a kernel; a kernel is an ideal, and the only ideals of a field are the field itself and (0).
column2: 我刚才应该讲清楚：域同态永远是单射，因为记住同态有一个核；核是一个理想，而一个域仅有的理想就是域本身与零理想 (0)。

column1: It can't be the field, because the homomorphism has to take 1 to 1; therefore the kernel has to be (0).
column2: 核不能是全域，因为同态必须把 1 映为 1；所以核必须是 (0)。

column1: Since the kernel is an ideal and the only ideals are (0) and (1), homomorphisms of fields are always injective! So it always factors injectively through the quotient field. So this is a nice characterization of what the quotient field is.
column2: 既然核是理想，而仅有的理想只有 (0) 和 (1)，域同态就必然是单射！所以它总是单射地分解经过商域。这是关于商域是什么的绝妙刻画。

column1: But then you still have to prove that such a field exists, so you have to go through the fraction construction.
column2: 但之后你依然必须证明这样一个域的存在性，所以必须经历分式构造过程。

column1: But once you've gone through it, I'll show you that any homomorphism to a field factors through the quotient field.
column2: 而一旦你完成了构造，我就能证明任何到域的同态都分解经过商域。

column1: Let's call this homomorphism h; and I have to tell you what this induced homomorphism is: let's call this map h^*, the map that I have to construct. So the definition of h^*: well, I have to tell you what h^* is on an equivalence class of fractions a/b, right?
column2: 我们把原同态记为 h；我必须告诉你所构造的诱导同态是什么：设这个我们要构造的映射为 h^*。那么 h^* 的定义为：我必须说明 h^* 作用在分式等价类 a/b 上是什么，对吧？

column1: I know what h(a) is, I know what h(b) is; so why don't I just define this as h(a) * h(b)^{-1}?

column1: Because I'm in a field, so whatever h(b) is, it's invertible if b != 0: since b != 0, h(b) is also not equal to 0, because h is an injective homomorphism!
column2: 因为我在域中，所以只要 b ≠ 0，h(b) 就必定可逆：因为 b ≠ 0，h(b) 也绝不等于0，因为 h 是单同态！

column1: So if we define a new homomorphism h^*, you find that the original map factors through it; and in some sense that shows that the quotient field is the smallest field that can contain a domain.
column2: 因此如果我们在这里定义一个新同态h^*，你就会发现原映射分解经过它；这在某种意义上表明商域是包含整环的最小的域。

column1: And it's a very, very useful object in a lot of manipulations of ring theory: using domains, you feel much more comfortable to think of them as sitting inside of a field; you may not have the inverse inside the domain, but you can go to this larger object where you can find the inverse.
column2: 在环论的许多推导中它是一个极其有用的工具：在研究整环时，将它们视作置于一个域内会让你踏实得多；在整环内部也许没有逆元，但你可以进入这个更大的对象并在其中找到逆元。
